extracted.intended_audience: researchers and institutions seeking American Heart Association cardiovascular/cerebrovascular research funding (trainees through senior investigators, data scientists, and institutional research offices)
extracted.subtask_description: Catalog of American Heart Association research funding opportunities with each program's purpose, eligibility emphasis, deadlines, and special requirements (e.g., pre-proposals, required collaborations, target career stage). Useful for investigators and institutional administrators preparing applications aligned to each award's goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-proposal / invitation-only requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Some programs require pre-proposals, with full proposals by invitation only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must monitor program pages for updates and deadlines; failure to submit a required pre-proposal will preclude invitation to submit a full proposal. See the Application Resources page for Heart Association policies, restrictions, and application preparation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator-Initiated Research (qualification based on career stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: For these funding opportunities, applicants initiate the research focus. Qualification for these awards is largely based on the principal investigator’s career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an investigator-initiated mechanism appropriate to the applicant's career phase (predoctoral, postdoctoral, early career, mid-career, etc.). Program-specific eligibility and expectations vary by award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-focused Funding (alignment to AHA strategic priorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs support specific areas of science deemed critical to achieving AHA mission and strategic objectives; the Association may co-fund projects with other organizations to advance common goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must align to the specified scientific topics and strategic priorities defined by each program; co-funding arrangements may bring additional expectations or partner requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Science Grants (global eligibility and career-stage inclusivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: These opportunities fund researchers from anywhere in the world working in data science and support investigators at all career stages, from trainees to senior scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data science proposals should demonstrate relevant expertise and applicability to cardiovascular/cerebrovascular research questions; international applicants are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registry Research (use of AHA Quality Programs data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators can submit proposals to conduct research using data from AHA Quality Programs' large national/regional registries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose analyses that leverage registry data; follow program-specific submission processes and data-use terms published under Quality Programs Research Using National-Level Data.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA Predoctoral Fellowship (training enhancement & career intent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhances the training of promising students in pre-doctoral or clinical health professional degree programs who intend careers as scientists, physician-scientists, or clinician-scientists, or related careers aimed at improving global health and wellbeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate commitment to research careers and propose training plans; note: some awards include additional collaboration funds from partner organizations (listed on program page). Proposal deadline example: Tuesday, August 4, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA Postdoctoral Fellowship (mentored postdoctoral training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhances training of postdoctoral applicants who are not yet independent; the applicant must be embedded in an appropriate investigative group with mentorship, support, and relevant scientific guidance of a research mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must include strong mentorship plans and institutional support. Some postdoctoral awards have additional designated collaboration funding from named partners. Example deadline: Wednesday, August 5, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Award for Undergraduate Student Training (institutional responsibility & meaningful research experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded to qualified institutions that can offer meaningful research experiences supporting the AHA mission and encourage undergraduate students from all disciplines to consider research careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are institutional (not individual) and must describe how the program will provide substantive training and exposure to research for undergraduates. Example deadline: Wednesday, September 9, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHA Institutional Research Enhancement Award (AIREA) (stimulating research at under-resourced institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stimulates research at educational institutions that provide baccalaureate or advanced degrees related to scientific research training and that may not have been major recipients of NIH support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible institutions should propose small-scale research projects related to cardiovascular diseases and brain health, aim to enhance the research environment, and expose students to research opportunities. Example deadline: Thursday, September 10, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Award (early professional appointment support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports highly promising healthcare and academic professionals in the early years of first professional appointment to assure the applicant’s future success as a research scientist in cardiovascular and/or cerebrovascular disease research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be in early faculty/clinical appointment and propose a development plan to transition toward research independence. Some awards include additional partner-designated funds. Example deadline: Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Visiting Professorship Award (short-term scientific exchange)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel pilot program to bring internationally based scientists to the U.S. for one week to foster scientific exchange and expand research experiences and collaborative opportunities for the Visiting Professor and their U.S.-based host in research that aligns with the AHA mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals/nomination should justify the visit's potential to foster collaborations and align clearly with AHA mission priorities. Note: proposal deadline for 2026 has passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative Project Award (novel, high-impact research not previously submitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports highly innovative, high-impact research that could lead to critical discoveries or major advancements; the idea proposed should not have been submitted in whole or in part in a previous proposal for AHA support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must emphasize novelty and potential high impact; prior submission (to AHA) of the same idea disqualifies the project. Some awards include partner-designated collaboration funds. Note: required pre-proposal deadline for 2026 has passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ralph L. Sacco Scholarships in Brain Health (mentored 2-year projects focused on prevention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enables early career trainees to undertake a mentored two-year research project targeting aspects of brain health; 2026 awards are for MD or PhD applicants in postdoctoral fellowship training with a focus on brain health and must focus on prevention with a clear connection to neurological or mental/behavioral health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be postdoctoral trainees (MD/PhD or equivalent) and propose mentored prevention-focused brain health projects that clearly connect to neurological or mental/behavioral health outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid Impact Research Award (topic-aligned innovative studies for early/mid-career investigators)
rubrics_metrics.description: For early- and mid-career investigators proposing innovative science studies aligned with sudden cardiac arrest/resuscitation science, Cardiovascular Kidney Metabolic (CKM) Syndrome, or stroke and/or vascular dementias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be early- or mid-career and propose innovative, focused projects aligned to the specified topical areas. Note: proposal deadline has passed for the listed cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redefining Women’s Health: From Heart to Head to Hormones (solicit ideas in priority areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invites researchers, clinicians, entrepreneurs and innovators to submit ideas to advance groundbreaking research and novel solutions in conditions that disproportionately or distinctly impact women’s health; four priority areas are described in program details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals/ideas must address one of the program's priority areas and aim for groundbreaking or novel solutions; consult program details for scope and submission expectations. Note: pre-proposal deadline has passed for the listed cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heart Transplantation Research Network (collaborative clinician-investigator network)
rubrics_metrics.description: A collaborative network of clinician investigators whose collective research efforts aim to enhance management options for patients undergoing heart transplantation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network proposals should demonstrate collaborative capacity across clinical investigators and a research agenda that will improve transplant patient management. Note: proposal deadline has passed for the listed cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cardiac Arrest Research Team (CART) Network (cross-border collaborative research)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AHA and partners establish a cross-border collaborative research network to address critical gaps in cardiac arrest and its consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be collaborative, often multinational, and target key knowledge gaps in cardiac arrest science. Note: required pre-proposal deadline has passed for the listed cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategically Focused Research Network (SFRN) on Earlier Detection and Delaying Progression of Valvular Heart Disease
rubrics_metrics.description: A strategically focused network with required pre-proposals to support collaborative research on earlier detection and delaying progression of valvular heart disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should center on detection and progression-delaying strategies and demonstrate network-level collaboration and impact. Note: required pre-proposal deadline has passed for the listed cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Science Grant — Using Real-World Data to Address Prevalence and Treatment in Cancer Patients and Survivors
rubrics_metrics.description: For multidisciplinary teams with expertise in two or more areas: cardio-oncology; CKM Syndrome; health economics; epidemiology; biostatistics with experience in causal inference methods, machine learning, and cardiovascular research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams must combine complementary expertise; proposed work should use real-world data to study prevalence and treatment patterns among cancer patients/survivors with cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic disease. Leverage appropriate data sources and methods for causal inference and ML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Science Grant — Identifying the Effects of GLP-1 Medications Among Individuals with CKM Disease and/or Obesity
rubrics_metrics.description: Research focused on evaluating effects of GLP-1 and/or GIP agonists among individuals with cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic disease (CKM) and/or obesity; applicants should have experience in causal inference methods, machine learning, and cardiovascular research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative, multidisciplinary proposals are encouraged; proposals are encouraged to leverage de-identified claims data, electronic health records, and prospective cohort studies as data sources. Note: deadline has passed for the listed cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of partner-designated collaboration funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Within several awards, additional collaboration money has been designated through partner organizations (e.g., AHA/CHF Congenital Heart Defect Research Awards, Autism Speaks, Barth Syndrome Foundation, California Walnut Commission, Foundation for Sarcoidosis Research, AHA/VIVA Physician Research Award, American Headache Society).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult specific program pages to determine partner-specific eligibility, expectations, and any additional application steps tied to these collaboration funds.
